statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-81870 (GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg, GO-2026-6505): in OpenTelemetry-Go 1.5.0 through 1.44.0, sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider emits an internal Info-level "TracerProvider created" event whose MarshalLog implementations recursively include the span processor, exporter and client configuration, so an application that enables OpenTelemetry's internal Info logging with otel.SetLogger can write OTLP gRPC and HTTP collector endpoints, the OTLP HTTP Insecure flag and complete Zipkin collector URLs to its logs; a Zipkin URL can carry credentials or tokens. The default OpenTelemetry logger does not emit the event. It is fixed in 1.45.0 by commit 3a1412d2b3bc4e4231fbeac2ed42117ae541bb38 (pull request 8438), whose changes outside tests, go.mod files and CHANGELOG.md are confined to the MarshalLog methods of the sdk/trace batch and simple span processors, the otlptrace exporter, the otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp clients and the zipkin exporter, which now log the span exporter and OTLP client as type-name strings and drop the endpoint, Insecure and URL fields: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6505, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/3a1412d2b3bc4e4231fbeac2ed42117ae541bb38, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8438, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/sdk/v1.45.0 . OSV lists no affected symbols, so we checked the functions that commit changes. This owner covers the packages built from the DHI build recipe: build and build-dev in the DHI Alpine 3.23 main repository and build-fips and build-fips-dev in the DHI Alpine 3.23 security repository. We unpacked every published build of all four, 92 versions from 2.4.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0 (build-dev, build-fips and build-fips-dev start at 2.6.4-r0, and 2.6.4-r0 was published for aarch64 only), for x86_64 and aarch64, and checked every download against the index checksum. The index lists 2.19.1-r1 three times per package and architecture with different checksums; the repository serves one file for each, which matches one of those entries and is the one we scanned. The ELF files are /usr/bin/build in every build (/opt/docker/dhi/build in 2.4.4-r0), plus, in build and build-fips only, /usr/bin/dhi-source from 2.28.0-r1, /opt/docker/dhi/yq from 2.26.2-r1 (all Go programs) and the Rust program /opt/docker/dhi/uv from 2.27.1-r1. For every Go ELF file we read the Go build information and the function table (from the Go line table, which also works on stripped binaries), and found runtime.main in each as a control, and we searched the raw bytes of every ELF file, which also catches inlined function names. The build information lists go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk (v1.38.0 to v1.47.0), but no function table contains any of the six MarshalLog methods the fix changes or sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider, which emits the event; the only sdk/trace functions present are package initialisers (sdk/trace.init, sdk/trace/internal/x.init and sdk/trace/internal/observ.init). The byte search found none of those methods' package-qualified names (the only MarshalLog methods in any function table are those of go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute.Set), no go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider string, none of the Go type names those methods return (pre-fix or fixed form) and no go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/ string at all, so no OTLP or Zipkin trace exporter is linked. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search run on a program we built against OpenTelemetry-Go v1.44.0 (sdk/trace with the otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp exporters) for amd64 and arm64 found the batch and simple span processor, otlptrace exporter and both client MarshalLog methods, sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider and the pre-fix type names. The code that emits the configuration is not in these packages.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-81870 (GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg): in OpenTelemetry-Go 1.5.0 to 1.44.0, creating an SDK TracerProvider records an internal Info-level diagnostic that includes the trace exporter's configuration: the OTLP collector endpoint (and the Insecure flag for OTLP/HTTP) or the full Zipkin collector URL. It is emitted only when the application installs a verbose internal logger with otel.SetLogger. The affected modules are go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk, exporters/otlp/otlptrace, exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc, exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp and exporters/zipkin before 1.45.0: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg, fix https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/3a1412d2b3bc4e4231fbeac2ed42117ae541bb38 (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8438), released in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/sdk/v1.45.0 . The fix stops the sdk/trace span processors and the otlptrace exporter from logging exporter and client internals, and removes the endpoint from the otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp clients' MarshalLog output. Checked every published caddy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 2026-11-27: 23 builds, 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.9-r5, each for x86_64 and aarch64. The Alpine 3.24 packages have the same index checksums as the Alpine 3.23 ones, and each package was downloaded, matched to its index checksum and read. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/caddy, a Go program built for GOOS=linux with no program interpreter or shared-library dependencies. We read each program's Go build information and its full function table from the Go line table, with runtime.main as a control. Every build contains sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider and the MarshalLog methods of the sdk/trace batch span processor, the otlptrace exporter and the otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp clients; no build contains the Zipkin exporter. OpenTelemetry module versions per build: 2.11.4-r0 has sdk and otlptrace 1.44.0 and otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp 1.43.0; 2.11.4-r1 to 2.11.4-r6 have sdk and otlptrace 1.45.0, otlptracehttp 1.45.0 and otlptracegrpc 1.43.0; 2.11.4-r7 to 2.11.4-r9 have sdk and otlptrace 1.46.0, otlptracehttp 1.45.0 and otlptracegrpc 1.43.0; 2.11.4-r10 has sdk and otlptrace 1.46.0 and otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp 1.45.0; 2.11.7-r0 to 2.11.9-r1 have 1.46.0 for all four; 2.11.9-r2 to 2.11.9-r5 have sdk 1.47.0 and 1.46.0 for the other three. 2.11.4-r1 to 2.11.4-r9 carry the sdk/trace and otlptrace parts of the fix but still ship otlptracegrpc 1.43.0, which the advisory lists as affected and whose client MarshalLog still includes the endpoint, so they carry only part of the fix and stay on the affected side. 2.11.4-r10 is the first build in which all four modules are 1.45.0 or later, and every later build ships 1.46.0 or later for all four, so 2.11.4-r10 is the first fixed build.

This owner covers the packages built from the Alpine docker recipe: docker, docker-engine, docker-cli and their support subpackages. We unpacked every subpackage of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 39 versions from 29.4.0-r1 to 29.10.0-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64 (29.4.3-r0 has no x86_64 docker-engine package), and checked every download against the index checksum. The only ELF files are three Go programs: /usr/bin/dockerd and /usr/bin/docker-proxy in docker-engine, and /usr/bin/docker in docker-cli. Reading their function tables (from the Go line table, with runtime.main as a control): dockerd contains the batch and simple span processor, otlptrace exporter, otlptracegrpc client and otlptracehttp client MarshalLog methods and sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider in every build; docker contains the batch span processor, otlptrace exporter and otlptracegrpc client MarshalLog methods and sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider in every build; docker-proxy contains none of them. So the status follows the module version. dockerd's Go build information shows go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace at v1.42.0 to v1.44.0 in every build up to 29.7.2-r3, and at v1.46.0 or v1.47.0 from 29.8.0-r0. The docker CLI is built from the vendor directory of the docker/cli release of the same version, and its build information records module versions only in 29.10.0-r1 (v1.47.0); docker/cli's vendor/modules.txt lists both modules at v1.42.0 to v1.44.0 for every release this repository ships up to v29.7.2 and at v1.46.0 or v1.47.0 for v29.8.0 to v29.10.0: https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/v29.7.2/vendor/modules.txt, https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/v29.8.0/vendor/modules.txt . As a check on the boundary, we searched the raw bytes of the dockerd and docker binaries in every build, on both architectures, for the Go type names of the values these methods return: the pre-fix forms (struct { Type string; SpanExporter trace.SpanExporter; ... }, struct { Type string; Client otlptrace.Client } and struct { Type string; Endpoint string }) are present in every build up to 29.7.2-r3 and absent from every build from 29.8.0-r0, which carry only the fixed forms (SpanExporter string, Client string). FIXED at 29.8.0-r0.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-81870 (GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg, GO-2026-6505): in OpenTelemetry-Go 1.5.0 to 1.44.0, sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider emits an internal Info-level log event whose MarshalLog methods include the span processor, exporter and client configuration, so an application that enables OpenTelemetry's internal Info logging with otel.SetLogger can record OTLP gRPC and HTTP collector endpoints and full Zipkin collector URLs, with any credentials embedded in them: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg. It is fixed in 1.45.0 by https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/3a1412d2b3bc4e4231fbeac2ed42117ae541bb38 (pull request 8438), whose changes outside tests, go.mod files and CHANGELOG.md are to the MarshalLog methods of the sdk/trace batch and simple span processors, the otlptrace Exporter, the otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp clients and the Zipkin exporter. The Go vulnerability database lists no affected symbols for this entry, so we searched for the functions that fix changes and for the NewTracerProvider entry point. The vulnerable code is not in this package. We downloaded every package built from the metrics-server source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: metrics-server and metrics-server-dev from the main repository and metrics-server-fips and metrics-server-fips-dev from the security repository, each 0.8.1-r0 through the current 0.9.1-r2 (29 builds), for x86_64 and aarch64, 232 package files, each checked against its repository index checksum and data hash. Each holds one file and no symbolic links: /usr/bin/metrics-server, a statically linked Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0, with no module replacements. Its build information lists go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk v1.40.0 to v1.47.0, otlptrace v1.35.0 to v1.47.0 and otlptracegrpc v1.35.0 to v1.45.0, but the Go function table of every build contains no function of the go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace package and none of the otlptrace, otlptracegrpc, otlptracehttp or Zipkin exporter packages, so no NewTracerProvider and no MarshalLog method of a span processor, exporter or client. The only functions under those module paths are package initializers (init functions) of sdk/trace/internal/observ and sdk/internal/x in every build, of otlptracegrpc/internal/x from 0.9.0-r0 and of sdk/internal/attrnorm from 0.9.0-r8, plus functions of sdk/resource. Its function table (read from the Go line table, with runtime.main as a control) contains the batch span processor, otlptrace exporter, otlptracegrpc client and otlptracehttp client MarshalLog methods and sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider in every build, so the status follows the module version. Its Go build information shows go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace at v1.44.0 in every build up to 5.5.0-3, and at v1.46.0 or later in every build from 5.5.1-0 (from 5.7.1-11 the sdk module is at v1.47.0 while otlptrace stays at v1.46.0). As a check on the boundary, we searched the raw bytes of the program in every build, on both architectures, for the Go type names of the values these methods return: the pre-fix forms (struct { Type string; SpanExporter trace.SpanExporter; ... }, struct { Type string; Client otlptrace.Client } and struct { Type string; Endpoint string }) are present in every build up to 5.5.0-3 and absent from every build from 5.5.1-0, which carry only the fixed forms (SpanExporter string, Client string). FIXED at 5.5.1-0.

CVE-2026-81870 (GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg, GO-2026-6505): in OpenTelemetry-Go 1.5.0 through 1.44.0, sdk/trace.NewTracerProvider emits an internal Info-level "TracerProvider created" event whose MarshalLog implementations recursively include the span processor, exporter and client configuration, so an application that enables OpenTelemetry's internal Info logging with otel.SetLogger can write OTLP gRPC and HTTP collector endpoints, the OTLP HTTP Insecure flag and complete Zipkin collector URLs to its logs; a Zipkin URL can carry credentials or tokens. The default OpenTelemetry logger does not emit the event. It is fixed in 1.45.0 by commit 3a1412d2b3bc4e4231fbeac2ed42117ae541bb38 (pull request 8438), whose changes outside tests, go.mod files and CHANGELOG.md are confined to the MarshalLog methods of the sdk/trace batch and simple span processors, the otlptrace exporter, the otlptracegrpc and otlptracehttp clients and the zipkin exporter, which now log the span exporter and OTLP client as type-name strings and drop the endpoint, Insecure and URL fields: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-8wmf-6v46-5gfg, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6505, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/3a1412d2b3bc4e4231fbeac2ed42117ae541bb38, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8438, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/sdk/v1.45.0 .
